source_note: Gale positions: MSL PLACES localized rover pose on the investigation sol (target within ~2 m). Global: USGS SIM 3292 landing-site layer. Work minutes and measurements are crewed-EVA planning assumptions.

gale.name: Jake Matijevic rock
gale.why: First rock Curiosity examined with its contact instruments; its alkaline, feldspar-rich composition was unlike any igneous rock seen before on Mars, showing that Gale's source magmas were more varied than expected.
gale.measure: Close-up imaging and handheld X-ray fluorescence of a cleaned surface; collect a hand sample.

sources.label: Stolper et al. 2013, Science 341, 'The Petrochemistry of Jake_M'
NASA JPL: Curiosity touches its first rock

gale.name: Bathurst Inlet
gale.why: Dark, fine-grained rock checked with the hand lens imager and APXS on the approach to Glenelg; a reference for the basaltic rocks around Bradbury Landing.
gale.measure: Hand-lens imaging of grain size and layering; X-ray fluorescence for composition.

sources.label: NASA: Curiosity Mars rover checks odd-looking rock (sol 54)

gale.name: Rocknest sand shadow
gale.why: Where Curiosity first scooped soil (sols 61-100). CheMin returned the first X-ray diffraction of Martian soil: basaltic minerals plus a large amorphous, water-bearing component.
gale.measure: Scoop and sieve windblown sand; bag samples for mineralogy and volatile analysis.

sources.label: Bish et al. 2013, Science 341, X-ray diffraction results from Rocknest
NASA: Rover's first soil studies help fingerprint Martian minerals

global.name: Viking 1 Landing Site
global.why: First successful U.S. landing (1976); Chryse Planitia outflow-channel plains and the Viking biology experiments.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: Viking 2 Landing Site
global.why: Utopia Planitia plains; observed seasonal surface frost.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: Mars Pathfinder Landing Site
global.why: Ares Vallis flood deposits; first Mars rover (Sojourner) measured rock chemistry.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: MER Spirit Landing Site
global.why: Spirit, Gusev crater: hydrothermal silica and carbonate-bearing outcrops in the Columbia Hills.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: MER Opportunity Landing Site
global.why: Opportunity, Meridiani Planum: hematite concretions and sulfate sandstones recording ancient water.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: Phoenix Landing Site
global.why: Phoenix: dug into ground ice and measured perchlorate in the soil at high northern latitude.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.

global.name: MSL Curiosity Landing Site (prelim)
global.why: Curiosity, Gale crater: ancient lake deposits and the layered foothills of Aeolis Mons.
global.measure: Context imaging, regolith sample and comparison with the mission's published results.
